plain_english: By whose opening and closing the worlds dissolve and emerge — to him, source of power-wheel glory, I praise Śaṅkara.
sanskrit_cite: yasyonmeṣanimeṣābhyāṃ jagataḥ pralayodayau | taṃ śakticakravibhavaprabhavaṃ śaṅkaraṃ stumaḥ

plain_english: Where this whole effect abides, and whence it has come forth — from being uncovered in form, there is no obstruction anywhere.
sanskrit_cite: yatra sthitam idaṃ sarvaṃ kāryaṃ yasmāc ca nirgataṃ | tasyānāvṛtarūpatvān na nirodho 'sti kutracit

plain_english: Even in the difference of waking and the rest, it glides in the undifferent; the perceiver-ness never turns back from its own being.
sanskrit_cite: jāgradādi vibhede 'pi tadabhinne prasarpati | nivartate nijānnaiva svabhāvād upalabdhṛtaḥ

plain_english: I happy, suffering, attached, and the like — those awarenesses plainly abide elsewhere, strung on pleasure-states.
sanskrit_cite: ahaṃ sukhī ca duḥkhī ca raktaś ca ityadisamvidaḥ | sukhādyavasthānusyūte vartante 'nyatra tāḥ sphuṭam

plain_english: Where there is no suffering, no joy, no graspable, no grasper, and not even delusion — THAT is, ultimately.
sanskrit_cite: na duḥkhaṃ na sukhaṃ yatra na grāhyam grāhakaṃ na ca | na cāsti mūḍhabhāvo 'pi tad asti paramārthataḥ

plain_english: Since the sense-host, deluded, thinks itself undeluded — forthgoing, standing, dissolving, by the inner wheel.
sanskrit_cite: yataḥ karaṇavargo 'yaṃ vimūḍho 'mūḍhavat svayam | sahāntareṇa cakreṇa pravṛttisthitisaṃhṛtiḥ
